messages:
liam: ran a long nsys capture on the reproduction load and noticed intermittent matmul workspace spikes that correlate with cuBLASLt choosing algo 0 and a big workspace (~500MB). spikes only happen under midbatch concurrent requests :eyes:
liam: paste of short timeline (trimmed):
```
[nsys timeline]
matmul_dispatch (shape 1x2048x2048): 0.9ms
cublasLt_matmul (algo=0, workspace=524288000): 31.4ms <-- spike
cublasLt_matmul (algo=5, workspace=65536): 1.2ms
KV cache hit: false
Batch sizes: 1,2,4 interleaved
```
liam: full nsys: https://artifacts.redwood/ci/2101234567/matmul-nsys.qdrep
liam: trying to figure out whether this is algoselection instability or workspace pressure causing fallback. any quick ideas?
maya: hmm looks like workspace request jumps when shapes are rounded to some internal tiling. could be cuBLASLt probing a workspace-heavy algo on certain concurrency and then falling back due to memory fragmentation :thinking_face:
maya: can you repro with KV cache disabled? maybe prefix caching changes memory layout and fragmentation timing. try REDWOOD_KVCACHE_PREFETCH=0 for a run
sam: add to that: run a single-threaded run to see if concurrency triggers a different algo. also try pinning max workspace to small value to force cheaper algos and observe perf curve
liam: repro steps I used: `nsys profile -o /tmp/m.nsrg --trace=cuda,cublas,cudnn --sample=none python -m tests.perf.run_matmul --shapes 1x2048x2048 --concurrency 3 --duration 120`
liam: also grabbed cublasLt logs by enabling our internal logging wrap (see attached logs)
rachel: did you capture timeline with nvtx spans? if you can add `nvtx_range_start` around matmul and prefix/cache operations, that helps isolate if the KV cache eviction happens right before the large ws allocation
liam: good call. I have a perfetto slice too: https://perfetto.redwood/trace/abcd1234 (shows mempool churn at 00:12:43 and matmul spike immediately after)
perf-bot: nsys analysis complete — report: /artifacts/2101234567/nsys-report.html (hotspot: cublasLtMatmul, 42% of GPU time in algorithm selection and workspace alloc path)
maya: if the hotspot is in the algorithm search, try caching the chosen algorithm per shape+dtype and replaying. we had a heuristic where we memoize cuBLASLt algos for the first N warmups
sam: suggestion: re-run with smaller batch window to avoid interleaving shapes. also test with `CUBLASLT_ALGO_CACHE=1` in our local test harness (that will force deterministic reuse of previously selected algos)
liam: quick experiment: forced single algo (algo=5) for that shape — consistent 1.1ms matmuls, no 30ms spikes. but we need an automated way to choose a safe default for the fleet, not manual pinning
rachel: can you also try with `CUDA_MALLOC_ASYNC=1` on/off? async allocator changes fragmentation characteristics and can hide workspace growth 
liam: will run both. planning: (1) repro with KV cache off, (2) single-threaded, (3) async malloc toggle, (4) algorithm memoization enabled. will post results in this thread tomorrow morning
maya: ack, also dump `nvidia-smi -q` and driver/cuda versions in that run — matching envs matters for cuBLASLt heuristic differences
sam: if you hit this in prod we can add a transient fallback: if matmul algo picks workspace > X bytes, force a cheaper candidate for the current request and record telemetry. avoid whole-request retry unless necessary
liam: good plan. one more log snippet I pasted from the capture showing the allocation failure path:
```
[workspace_request] requested=524288000 available_pool=420000000 => fallback path triggered
[cublasLt] probe algos: 0(ws=524288000), 3(ws=1048576), 5(ws=65536)
selected alg=0 -> then memory alloc failed -> fallback to alg=5 afterwards
```
liam: thanks all, will run the matrix and update. tagging @maya @sam for followups :rocket:
